expo.name: Doorway

//: ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption declared false, because this app uses only the
HTTPS the platform provides and Apple's own exemption covers that. Declaring
it here answers the export-compliance question once instead of at every
submission, and answering it carelessly under release pressure is how a build
sits in review for a week.
No NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription and no NSCameraUsageDescription, because the
mobile app does not take or attach photos — media is uploaded from the web app.
A usage string for a permission the app never requests invites a reviewer to
ask why, and the honest answer would be 'it does not'.
No `permissions` array. expo-notifications adds POST_NOTIFICATIONS itself, and
a hand-written list here would drift from what the plugins actually need. There
is no location, camera, microphone, contacts or storage permission in this app.

extra.//: One binary serves every centre. The tenant is resolved at sign-in, never baked into the build — which is the whole reason this platform is pooled rather than one deployment per customer.

//: MISSING AND REQUIRED BEFORE ANY STORE SUBMISSION. Listed here rather than
referenced as file paths that do not exist — a config pointing at a missing icon
fails the build with an error about a file, not about the decision:
• icon, 1024×1024, no transparency and no pre-rounded corners (Apple rejects both)
• android.adaptiveIcon, foreground plus background, 108dp with a 66dp safe circle
• a splash screen via expo-splash-screen
• an Android notification icon, or the system draws a grey square
docs/store-listing.md holds everything else a submission needs, including the Play
Data Safety answers and Apple's privacy questionnaire — both written out there,
because both are declarations about children's data and both are easy to answer
carelessly.
